\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter04.Parity}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Flipping a coordinate reverses full parity]
\lean{FABL.parityFunction_univ_flipCoordinate}
\label{FABL.parityFunction_univ_flipCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.setCoordinate}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, every Boolean-cube input $x$, and every coordinate $i$,
flipping coordinate $i$ reverses the full parity: the parity over all $n$ coordinates at
the flipped input is the negative of its value at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Every coordinate is pivotal for full parity]
\lean{FABL.parityFunction_univ_isPivotal}
\label{FABL.parityFunction_univ_isPivotal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsPivotal, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.parityFunction_univ_flipCoordinate}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$, every Boolean-cube input $x$, and every coordinate $i$,
coordinate $i$ is pivotal for the parity function on all $n$ coordinates: flipping it
changes the function's value.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Term width for parity]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.term_width_eq_dimension_of_computes_parity}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b009}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.term_width_eq_dimension_of_computes_parity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.eval, FABL.DNFFormula.eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.DNFTerm.satisfyingEquiv, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.DNFTerm.width_le_dimension, FABL.IsNegOnePivotal, FABL.Sign, FABL.card_negOnePivotal_le_term_width, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.parityFunction_univ_isPivotal}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\varphi$ be a DNF formula on $n$ sign coordinates, and
suppose its Boolean function equals the parity function on all $n$ coordinates. Every
term $T$ in $\varphi$ has width $n$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
For every positive natural number $n$, the parity function on all $n$ coordinates is
balanced on the Boolean cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Negative values of full parity occur half the time]
\lean{FABL.parityFunction_univ_neg_one_probability}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p023-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p025-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p026-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p026-b007
}
\label{FABL.parityFunction_univ_neg_one_probability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.isBalanced_iff_uniformProbability_one_eq_half, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.parityFunction_univ_isBalanced, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability_one_add_neg_one_eq_one}
\difficulty{4}
For every positive natural number $n$, the uniform probability that the parity function
on all $n$ coordinates takes the value $-1$ is $1/2$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
For every positive integer $n$, the minterm disjunctive normal form of the parity
function on all $n$ coordinates of the sign cube has size $2^{n-1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform probability bound for DNF evaluation]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.uniformProbability_eval_neg_one_le_term_sum}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.uniformProbability_eval_neg_one_le_term_sum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.eval, FABL.DNFFormula.eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.expect_sum_list_map, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability_DNFTerm_eval_neg_one}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $\varphi$ be a DNF formula on $n$ sign coordinates. Under
the uniform distribution on the sign cube, the probability that $\varphi$ evaluates to
$-1$ is at most the sum, over its terms $T$, of $2^{-\operatorname{width}(T)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity disjunctive normal form]
\lean{FABL.parityDNF}
\label{FABL.parityDNF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.mintermDNF, FABL.parityFunction}
For each natural number $n$, define the disjunctive normal form of parity on the $n$
coordinates to be the minterm DNF associated with the parity function on all
coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Parity DNF represents parity]
\lean{FABL.parityDNF_toBooleanFunction}
\label{FABL.parityDNF_toBooleanFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.mintermDNF_toBooleanFunction, FABL.parityDNF, FABL.parityFunction}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, the Boolean function represented by the minterm DNF of
parity on all $n$ coordinates equals parity on all $n$ coordinates; explicitly, its
value at $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$ is $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Size of the parity DNF]
\lean{FABL.size_parityDNF}
\label{FABL.size_parityDNF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula.size, FABL.parityDNF, FABL.size_mintermDNF_parityFunction_univ}
\difficulty{1}
For every positive integer $n$, the disjunctive normal form consisting of one minterm
for each input on which parity on $n$ coordinates equals $-1$ has exactly $2^{n-1}$
terms.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
For every positive integer $n$, the minimum number of terms in a DNF representing the
parity function $x\mapsto\prod_{i=1}^n x_i$ on $\{\pm1\}^n$ is $2^{n-1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of the Boolean dual]
\lean{FABL.mean_booleanDual}
\label{FABL.mean_booleanDual}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual, FABL.mean, FABL.signCubeNegEquiv, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
For any Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, define its dual by
$f^*(x)=-f(-x)$, where negation is applied to every input coordinate. The mean of the
real-valued function associated to $f^*$ is the negative of the mean associated to $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Balance under Boolean duality]
\lean{FABL.isBalanced_booleanDual}
\label{FABL.isBalanced_booleanDual}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual, FABL.IsBalanced, FABL.mean_booleanDual}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and suppose its
real-valued form has mean zero under the uniform distribution. The function obtained by
negating the output of $f$ at the coordinatewise negation of its input also has mean
zero under the uniform distribution.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Minterm DNF size of a balanced function]
\lean{FABL.size_mintermDNF_of_isBalanced}
\label{FABL.size_mintermDNF_of_isBalanced}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.DNFFormula.size, FABL.IsBalanced, FABL.Sign, FABL.mintermDNF, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability_neg_one_eq_half_of_isBalanced}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional sign cube to $\{
-1,1\}$. If the uniform mean of the real-valued sign of $f$ is zero, then the minterm
disjunctive normal form formed from the inputs on which $f$ equals $-1$ has size
$2^{n-1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Injectivity of Boolean duality]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual_injective}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual_injective}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual}
\difficulty{3}
For a natural number $n$, the operation that sends a sign-valued Boolean function $f$ on
the $n$-dimensional sign cube to the function $x\mapsto -f(-x)$ is injective.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Pivotality of the dual parity function]
\lean{FABL.booleanDual_parityFunction_univ_isPivotal}
\label{FABL.booleanDual_parityFunction_univ_isPivotal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual, FABL.IsPivotal, FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.parityFunction_univ_flipCoordinate, FABL.setCoordinate}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, and choose a coordinate $i$. The
Boolean dual of the parity function on all $n$ coordinates takes different values at $x$
and at the vector obtained by flipping coordinate $i$ of $x$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\varphi$ be a DNF formula on $n$ sign coordinates, and
suppose its Boolean function equals the Boolean dual of the parity function on all $n$
coordinates. Every term $T$ in $\varphi$ has width $n$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
Let $\psi$ be a CNF formula on $n$ variables whose Boolean function equals the parity
function on all $n$ coordinates. Every clause appearing in $\psi$ has width exactly
$n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity conjunctive normal form]
\lean{FABL.parityCNF}
\label{FABL.parityCNF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual, FABL.mintermDNF, FABL.parityFunction}
For each natural number $n$, define the conjunctive normal form of parity on the $n$
coordinates by taking the minterm DNF associated with the Boolean dual of the parity
function on all coordinates, and using its terms as the clauses.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Size of the parity CNF]
\lean{FABL.size_parityCNF}
\label{FABL.size_parityCNF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.DNFFormula.size, FABL.isBalanced_booleanDual, FABL.mintermDNF, FABL.parityCNF, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.parityFunction_univ_isBalanced, FABL.size_mintermDNF_of_isBalanced}
\difficulty{3}
For every positive integer $n$, the conjunctive normal form obtained by taking one
clause for each satisfying input of the Boolean dual of parity on $n$ coordinates has
exactly $2^{n-1}$ clauses.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Parity CNF represents parity]
\lean{FABL.parityCNF_toBooleanFunction}
\label{FABL.parityCNF_toBooleanFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual, FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual_injective, FABL.CNFFormula.switchAndOr_toBooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.mintermDNF, FABL.mintermDNF_toBooleanFunction, FABL.parityCNF, FABL.parityFunction}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, the Boolean function represented by the CNF formed from
the minterm DNF of the dual of parity on all $n$ coordinates equals parity on all $n$
coordinates; explicitly, its value at $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$ is $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity block assignment]
\lean{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
For a nonnegative integer $r$, a parity block assignment is a function assigning to each
of the $r$ coordinates a sign, viewed as a unit of the integers.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Parity block assignments]
\lean{FABL.card_parityBlockAssignment}
\label{FABL.card_parityBlockAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $r$, the set of assignments of a sign in $\{ -1,1 \}$ to each
of $r$ positions has cardinality $2^r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity block assignment equivalence]
\lean{FABL.parityBlockAssignmentEquiv}
\label{FABL.parityBlockAssignmentEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.card_parityBlockAssignment}
For every natural number $r$, there is an equivalence between the set of integers from
$0$ to $2^r-1$ and the set of assignments of a sign to each of the $r$ coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Parity block product]
\lean{FABL.parityBlockProduct}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityBlockProduct}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.Sign}
For a nonnegative integer $r$ and an assignment of a sign to each of its $r$
coordinates, define the parity block product to be the product of those signs.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Parity block slots]
\lean{FABL.parityBlockSlots}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityBlockSlots}
\leanok
For nonnegative integers $n$, $r$, and $g$, the parity block slots are the indices $j$
with $0\leq j<r$ for which $gr+j<n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate in a parity block]
\lean{FABL.parityBlockCoordinate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityBlockCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityBlockSlots}
For natural numbers $n,r,g$, the parity block consists of the indices $g r+j$ that are
less than $n$, with $0\le j<r$. The coordinate associated to such a $j$ is the index $g
r+j$ in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Injectivity of the parity block coordinate map]
\lean{FABL.parityBlockCoordinate_injective}
\label{FABL.parityBlockCoordinate_injective}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityBlockCoordinate}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,r,g$ be natural numbers, and let $J=\{j\in\{0,\ldots,r-1\}:gr+j<n\}$. The map
$J\to\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ sending $j$ to $gr+j$ is injective.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity block minterm]
\lean{FABL.parityBlockMinterm}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityBlockMinterm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityBlockCoordinate, FABL.parityBlockCoordinate_injective, FABL.parityBlockSlots}
For natural numbers $n,r,g$ and an assignment $a$ of signs to the $r$ positions, form a
conjunction with one literal for each $j<r$ such that $g r+j<n$. The literal uses
coordinate $g r+j$ and requires the sign $a(j)$; all literal coordinates are distinct.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Value on a parity block]
\lean{FABL.parityBlockValue}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityBlockValue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment}
For natural numbers $n,r,g$ and a sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, define an assignment of
signs to the $r$ positions by assigning to position $j$ the coordinate of $x$ at index
$gr+j$ if $gr+j<n$, and assigning $1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Valid parity block assignment]
\lean{FABL.IsValidParityBlockAssignment}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.IsValidParityBlockAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment}
For natural numbers $n,r,g$, an assignment $a$ of signs to the $r$ positions is valid
if, for every $j<r$ with $n\le g r+j$, its sign is $a(j)=1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Normalization of a parity block assignment]
\lean{FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment}
\label{FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment}
Given natural numbers $n$, $r$, and $g$, and a function $a$ assigning a sign to each
index $j\in\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$, define a new assignment whose value at $j$ is $a(j)$ if
$gr+j<n$, and is $1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Validity of the normalized assignment]
\lean{FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment_valid}
\label{FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment_valid}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsValidParityBlockAssignment, FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,r,g$ be nonnegative integers, and let $a$ assign a sign to each index $j$ with
$0\le j<r$. After retaining $a(j)$ when $gr+j<n$ and assigning $1$ otherwise, the
resulting assignment has value $1$ at every index $j$ for which $n\le gr+j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Normalization of a valid parity block assignment]
\lean{FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment_eq_self}
\label{FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment_eq_self}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsValidParityBlockAssignment, FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,r,g$ be nonnegative integers, and let $a$ assign a sign to each index $j$ with
$0\le j<r$. Suppose that whenever $n\le gr+j$, the assigned sign $a(j)$ is $1$. Then
normalizing $a$ by retaining its value at indices with $gr+j<n$ and assigning $1$ at all
other indices leaves $a$ unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Validity of parity block values]
\lean{FABL.parityBlockValue_valid}
\label{FABL.parityBlockValue_valid}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsValidParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityBlockValue}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,r,g$ be natural numbers, let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, and define the block assignment by
taking its $j$th entry to be $x_{gr+j}$ when $gr+j<n$ and $1$ otherwise. Every entry
whose index satisfies $n\le gr+j$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of a parity block minterm]
\lean{FABL.parityBlockMinterm_eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.parityBlockMinterm_eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.DNFTerm.eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.Literal, FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityBlockCoordinate, FABL.parityBlockMinterm, FABL.parityBlockSlots, FABL.parityBlockValue}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n,r,g$ be natural numbers, let $a$ assign a sign in $\{-1,1\}$ to each
$j\in\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$, and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. Form a conjunction of literals
requiring $x_{gr+j}=a_j$ for each $j<r$ with $gr+j<n$; a literal evaluates to $-1$ when
its required sign matches the input coordinate and to $1$ otherwise, and the conjunction
evaluates to $-1$ exactly when every literal does. Then this conjunction evaluates to
$-1$ if and only if the assignment $a$, replaced by $1$ at indices with $gr+j\ge n$,
agrees at every index with the block of input signs $x_{gr+j}$, using $1$ whenever
$gr+j\ge n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity layer size]
\lean{FABL.parityLayerSize}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityLayerSize}
\leanok
For natural numbers $r,q$, the parity layer size is $r^q 2^r$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Parity layer indexing bijection]
\lean{FABL.parityLayerEquiv}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityLayerEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityBlockAssignmentEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize}
For natural numbers $r,q$, there is a bijection between the indices $0\le i<r^q2^r$ and
pairs consisting of an index $0\le g<r^q$ and an assignment of signs to the $r$
positions.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Left inverse identity for layer indexing]
\lean{FABL.parityLayerEquiv_symm_apply_apply}
\label{FABL.parityLayerEquiv_symm_apply_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $r$ and $q$, applying the inverse of the layer equivalence to the
image of any index in $	ext{Fin}(r^q2^r)$ returns that index.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Right inverse identity for layer indexing]
\lean{FABL.parityLayerEquiv_apply_symm_apply}
\label{FABL.parityLayerEquiv_apply_symm_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityLayerEquiv}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $r$ and $q$, the layer equivalence from indices in a set of size
$r^q2^r$ to pairs consisting of a position in $	ext{Fin}(r^q)$ and a parity block
assignment is a right inverse to its inverse: applying the equivalence after its inverse
returns the original pair.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity child group bijection]
\lean{FABL.parityChildGroupEquiv}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityChildGroupEquiv}
\leanok
For natural numbers $r,q$, there is a bijection between pairs $(g,j)$ with $0\le g<r^q$
and $0\le j<r$, and indices $0\le k<r^{q+1}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Parity child group index]
\lean{FABL.parityChildGroup}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityChildGroup}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityChildGroupEquiv}
For natural numbers $r,q$, an index $g$ with $0\le g<r^q$, and an index $j$ with $0\le
j<r$, the parity child group is the index corresponding to the pair $(g,j)$ under the
bijection between such pairs and indices less than $r^{q+1}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Parity child group index formula]
\lean{FABL.parityChildGroup_val}
\label{FABL.parityChildGroup_val}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityChildGroup, FABL.parityChildGroupEquiv}
\difficulty{1}
Let $r,q$ be natural numbers, let $g$ be an index in $	ext{Fin}(r^q)$, and let $j$ be an
index in $	ext{Fin}(r)$. The index assigned to the pair $(g,j)$ in $	ext{Fin}(r^{q+1})$
has value $g r+j$, where $g$ and $j$ denote their respective values.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Injectivity of child group indexing]
\lean{FABL.parityChildGroup_injective}
\label{FABL.parityChildGroup_injective}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityChildGroup, FABL.parityChildGroupEquiv}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $r$ and $q$, the map sending a pair $(g,j)$, with $g<r^q$ and $j<r$,
to its child group index in the set of size $r^{q+1}$ is injective.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Padded parity input]
\lean{FABL.paddedParityInput}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.paddedParityInput}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
For a natural number $n$, a sign vector $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$, and an index $i\in\mathbb{N}$,
define the padded input to equal the $i$th coordinate of $x$ when $i<n$, and to equal
$1$ when $i\ge n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Parity tree value]
\lean{FABL.parityTreeValue}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityTreeValue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.paddedParityInput}
For natural numbers $n$ and $r$ and a sign vector $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$, define values at
levels $t\in\mathbb{N}$ and positions $g\in\mathbb{N}$ recursively: at level $0$, the
value is the padded input at position $g$; at level $t+1$, it is the product of the
level-$t$ values at positions $gr+j$ as $j$ ranges from $0$ to $r-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Base case for parity trees]
\lean{FABL.parityTreeValue_zero}
\label{FABL.parityTreeValue_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.paddedParityInput, FABL.parityTreeValue}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $n,r,g$ and $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, the depth-zero parity tree value at
index $g$ equals the padded input: it is $x_g$ when $g<n$ and $1$ when $g\ge n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Successor recursion for parity trees]
\lean{FABL.parityTreeValue_succ}
\label{FABL.parityTreeValue_succ}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityTreeValue}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $n,r,t,g$ and $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, the depth-$(t+1)$ parity tree value
at index $g$ is the product, over $j=0,\ldots,r-1$, of the depth-$t$ values at indices
$gr+j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity tree assignment]
\lean{FABL.parityTreeAssignment}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityTreeAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityTreeValue}
For natural numbers $n,r,t,g$ and a sign vector $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$, define an
$r$-coordinate assignment whose value at each $j\in\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$ is the parity tree
value for parameters $n,r,x,t$ at index $gr+j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Product of a parity tree assignment]
\lean{FABL.parityBlockProduct_treeAssignment}
\label{FABL.parityBlockProduct_treeAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityBlockProduct, FABL.parityTreeAssignment, FABL.parityTreeValue}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,r,t,g$ be natural numbers and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. The product of the $r$ signs
assigned by the parity tree at level $t$ to the indices $gr,gr+1,\ldots,gr+r-1$ equals
the parity tree value at level $t+1$ and index $g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Initial parity tree assignment]
\lean{FABL.parityTreeAssignment_zero_eq_blockValue}
\label{FABL.parityTreeAssignment_zero_eq_blockValue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.paddedParityInput, FABL.parityBlockValue, FABL.parityTreeAssignment}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,r,g$ be natural numbers and let $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$. The parity tree assignment at
level zero and group index $g$ equals the assignment whose $j$th coordinate is the $g
r+j$th coordinate of $x$ when $g r+j<n$, and is $1$ otherwise, for each
$j\in\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Exact parity node value]
\lean{FABL.parityExactNodeValue}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityExactNodeValue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitGate, FABL.Sign}
A gate is either AND or OR. Given such a gate and a Boolean match indicator, define the
node's sign to be $-1$ for a matching AND and for a nonmatching OR, and $1$ for a
nonmatching AND and for a matching OR.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[AND gate value on a match]
\lean{FABL.parityExactNodeValue_and_true}
\label{FABL.parityExactNodeValue_and_true}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityExactNodeValue}
\difficulty{1}
For an AND gate and a true match indicator, the parity exact node value is $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[False input to an AND gate]
\lean{FABL.parityExactNodeValue_and_false}
\label{FABL.parityExactNodeValue_and_false}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityExactNodeValue}
\difficulty{1}
The value assigned to an AND gate when its match indicator is false is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[OR gate value on a true match]
\lean{FABL.parityExactNodeValue_or_true}
\label{FABL.parityExactNodeValue_or_true}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityExactNodeValue}
\difficulty{1}
For an OR gate and a true match indicator, the parity exact node value is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[OR gate value on a false match]
\lean{FABL.parityExactNodeValue_or_false}
\label{FABL.parityExactNodeValue_or_false}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityExactNodeValue}
\difficulty{1}
For an OR gate and a false match indicator, the parity exact node value is $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity layer values]
\lean{FABL.parityLayerValues}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityLayerValues}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitGate, FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.Sign, FABL.parityExactNodeValue, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize}
For natural numbers $r,q$, a gate (AND or OR), and an actual assignment of a sign vector
to each of the $r^q$ groups, define a sign at each of the $r^q2^r$ layer positions as
follows. Decode the position into a group and a sign vector of length $r$; the value is
the exact node value for the chosen gate, with match meaning that this decoded vector
equals the actual assignment for that group.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[AND layer value characterisation]
\lean{FABL.parityLayerValues_and_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.parityLayerValues_and_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityExactNodeValue, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityLayerValues}
\difficulty{4}
Let $r,q$ be natural numbers, let the actual assignment at each position in
$	ext{Fin}(r^q)$ be a parity block assignment, and let $i$ be an index in
$	ext{Fin}(r^q2^r)$. The AND layer value at $i$ equals $-1$ if and only if the parity
block assignment in the pair corresponding to $i$ equals the actual assignment at that
pair's position.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[OR layer value characterisation]
\lean{FABL.parityLayerValues_or_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.parityLayerValues_or_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityExactNodeValue, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityLayerValues}
\difficulty{4}
Let $r,q$ be natural numbers, let the actual assignment at each position in
$	ext{Fin}(r^q)$ be a parity block assignment, and let $i$ be an index in
$	ext{Fin}(r^q2^r)$. The OR layer value at $i$ equals $-1$ if and only if the parity
block assignment in the pair corresponding to $i$ differs from the actual assignment at
that pair's position.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[OR layer value characterisation]
\lean{FABL.parityLayerValues_or_eq_one_iff}
\label{FABL.parityLayerValues_or_eq_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityExactNodeValue, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityLayerValues}
\difficulty{4}
Let $r,q$ be natural numbers, let the actual assignment at each position in
$	ext{Fin}(r^q)$ be a parity block assignment, and let $i$ be an index in
$	ext{Fin}(r^q2^r)$. The OR layer value at $i$ equals $1$ if and only if the parity
block assignment in the pair corresponding to $i$ equals the actual assignment at that
pair's position.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Next actual parity assignment]
\lean{FABL.parityNextActualAssignment}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityNextActualAssignment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityBlockProduct, FABL.parityChildGroup}
For natural numbers $r,q$, an assignment of a sign vector of length $r$ to each of the
$r^{q+1}$ groups, and a group $g$ among the $r^q$ groups, define the next actual
assignment at position $j$ to be the product of the signs in the assignment of the child
group indexed by $g$ and $j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Next parity node inputs]
\lean{FABL.parityNextNodeInputs}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityNextNodeInputs}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityBlockProduct, FABL.parityChildGroup, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize}
For natural numbers $r,q$, a group $g$ among the $r^q$ groups, and a sign assignment $a$
on $r$ positions, define a set of positions in the layer of size $r^{q+1}2^r$. It
consists of those positions which decode to a group of the form obtained from $g$ and
some $j\in\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$, and whose decoded sign vector has product different from
$a(j)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of next-node inputs]
\lean{FABL.mem_parityNextNodeInputs_iff}
\label{FABL.mem_parityNextNodeInputs_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityBlockProduct, FABL.parityChildGroup, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityNextNodeInputs}
\difficulty{1}
Let $r,q$ be natural numbers, let $g$ be an index in a set of size $r^q$, and let $a$
assign a sign in $\{\pm1\}$ to each of $r$ positions. An index $i$ in the layer of size
$r^{q+1}2^r$ belongs to the next-node input set for $(g,a)$ if and only if, under the
canonical indexing of that layer by a pair consisting of an index and a sign assignment,
there is a position $j$ such that the first component is the child index associated to
$(g,j)$ and the product of the signs in the second component differs from $a(j)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Distinct assignments differ at a coordinate]
\lean{FABL.exists_apply_ne_of_ne}
\label{FABL.exists_apply_ne_of_ne}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment}
\difficulty{3}
Let $r$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $a,b$ be assignments of signs to the $r$
coordinates. If $a$ and $b$ are distinct, then there is a coordinate $j$ at which their
assigned signs differ.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the next parity node inputs]
\lean{FABL.eval_parityNextNodeInputs}
\label{FABL.eval_parityNextNodeInputs}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitGate, FABL.CircuitGate.dual, FABL.CircuitGate.evalFinset, FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.exists_apply_ne_of_ne, FABL.mem_parityNextNodeInputs_iff, FABL.parityBlockProduct, FABL.parityChildGroup, FABL.parityExactNodeValue, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityLayerValues, FABL.parityLayerValues_and_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.parityLayerValues_or_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.parityNextActualAssignment, FABL.parityNextNodeInputs}
\difficulty{6}
Let $r,q$ be natural numbers, let $G$ be either an AND or OR gate, let $A$ assign a sign
block to each of the $r^{q+1}$ groups, let $g$ index one of $r^q$ groups, and let $a$ be
a sign assignment on $	ext{Fin}(r)$. Applying the gate dual to $G$ to the level-$q+1$
node values over the specified input set equals the exact dual-gate node value: it is
the matching value precisely when $a$ equals the assignment whose $j$th sign is the
product of the block $A$ assigns to child group $(g,j)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity first layer]
\lean{FABL.parityFirstLayer}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityFirstLayer}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.parityBlockMinterm, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize}
For natural numbers $n,r,q$, define a list of $r^q2^r$ terms in disjunctive normal form.
For each position in the list, decode it into a group and a sign vector, and take the
minterm on the $n$ variables specified by that group and sign vector.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Length of the First Parity Layer]
\lean{FABL.length_parityFirstLayer}
\label{FABL.length_parityFirstLayer}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityFirstLayer, FABL.parityLayerSize}
\difficulty{1}
For all natural numbers $n$, $r$, and $q$, the first parity layer has length $r^q 2^r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity bottom-layer values]
\lean{FABL.parityBottomLayerValues}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityBottomLayerValues}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityExactNodeValue, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityTreeAssignment}
For natural numbers $n,r,q$ and a sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, assign to each index in
a layer of size $r^q2^r$ the exact AND-node value obtained by comparing the normalized
block assignment at that index with the level-zero tree assignment determined by $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the first parity layer]
\lean{FABL.eval_parityFirstLayer}
\label{FABL.eval_parityFirstLayer}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitGate.evalTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.length_parityFirstLayer, FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityBlockMinterm, FABL.parityBlockMinterm_eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.parityBlockValue, FABL.parityBottomLayerValues, FABL.parityExactNodeValue, FABL.parityFirstLayer, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityTreeAssignment, FABL.parityTreeAssignment_zero_eq_blockValue}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n,r,q$ be natural numbers, let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, and choose an index $i$ in a layer
of size $r^q2^r$. The AND gate applied to the parity-block minterm at index $i$
evaluates to the corresponding bottom-layer value at $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity next layer]
\lean{FABL.parityNextLayer}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityNextLayer}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityNextNodeInputs}
For natural numbers $r$ and $q$, form a list with one entry for each index in a layer of
size $r^q2^r$. The entry at each index is the finite set of inputs to the corresponding
node in the next layer, whose size is $r^{q+1}2^r$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Length of the Next Parity Layer]
\lean{FABL.length_parityNextLayer}
\label{FABL.length_parityNextLayer}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityNextLayer}
\difficulty{1}
For all natural numbers $r$ and $q$, the next parity layer has length $r^q 2^r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Entries of the parity next layer]
\lean{FABL.get_parityNextLayer}
\label{FABL.get_parityNextLayer}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.length_parityNextLayer, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityNextLayer, FABL.parityNextNodeInputs}
\difficulty{1}
Let $r,q\in\mathbb N$, and let $i$ be an index in a layer of size $r^q2^r$. Under the
canonical indexing of that layer by pairs $(g,a)$, where $g\in\{0,\ldots,r^q-1\}$ and
$a$ assigns a sign $\pm1$ to each of the $r$ positions, the entry of the next-layer list
at index $i$ is the set of child indices corresponding to pairs $(h,b)$ for which there
is some $j\in\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$ such that $h$ is the child group of $g$ and $j$, and the
product of the signs in $b$ differs from $a(j)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity output inputs]
\lean{FABL.parityOutputInputs}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityOutputInputs}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitGate, FABL.parityBlockProduct, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize}
For a natural number $r$ and a choice of AND or OR, take the indices in a layer of size
$2^r$ whose associated sign assignment has product $-1$ for AND, or product different
from $-1$ for OR.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of AND output inputs]
\lean{FABL.mem_parityOutputInputs_and_iff}
\label{FABL.mem_parityOutputInputs_and_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityBlockProduct, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityOutputInputs}
\difficulty{1}
Let $r$ be a natural number, and index a layer of size $2^r$ by sign assignments to $r$
positions. An index $i$ belongs to the input set of the parity circuit's AND output if
and only if the product of the signs in the assignment corresponding to $i$ is $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Parity output membership]
\lean{FABL.mem_parityOutputInputs_or_iff}
\label{FABL.mem_parityOutputInputs_or_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityBlockProduct, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityOutputInputs}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $r$ and every index $i$ among the $2^r$ inputs, $i$ belongs to
the set of inputs selected by the OR gate exactly when the product of the signs in the
parity block assigned to $i$ is not $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the parity output inputs]
\lean{FABL.eval_parityOutputInputs}
\label{FABL.eval_parityOutputInputs}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitGate, FABL.CircuitGate.dual, FABL.CircuitGate.evalFinset, FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.Sign, FABL.mem_parityOutputInputs_and_iff, FABL.mem_parityOutputInputs_or_iff, FABL.parityBlockProduct, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityLayerValues, FABL.parityLayerValues_and_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.parityLayerValues_or_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.parityOutputInputs}
\difficulty{5}
Let $r$ be a natural number, let $G$ be either an AND or OR gate, and let $A$ assign a
sign block to each index in $	ext{Fin}(r^0)$. Applying the gate dual to $G$ to the
level-zero node values over the specified output input set equals the product of the
signs in the block assigned by $A$ to the unique index in $	ext{Fin}(r^0)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bottom layer value criterion]
\lean{FABL.parityBottomLayerValues_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.parityBottomLayerValues_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityBottomLayerValues, FABL.parityExactNodeValue, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityTreeAssignment}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,r,q$ be natural numbers, let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, and choose an index $i$ in a set
of size $r^q2^r$. Use the specified bijection to write $i$ as a pair consisting of a
group index $g<r^q$ and a sign assignment $a\in\{-1,1\}^r$. The corresponding bottom
layer value is $-1$ if and only if the assignment obtained from $a$ by replacing entries
beyond the input length with $1$ equals the block of $r$ input values starting at
position $g$, with out-of-range input values padded by $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Recursive parity assignment identity]
\lean{FABL.parityNextActualAssignment_tree}
\label{FABL.parityNextActualAssignment_tree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityChildGroup_val, FABL.parityNextActualAssignment, FABL.parityTreeAssignment}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,r,t,q$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a sign vector of length $n$, and let
$g\in\text{Fin}(r^q)$. At each child position of $g$, take the product of the signs in
the parity tree assignment at depth $t$; the resulting parity block assignment equals
the parity tree assignment at depth $t+1$ and position $g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity bottom next-node inputs]
\lean{FABL.parityBottomNextNodeInputs}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityBottomNextNodeInputs}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityBlockProduct, FABL.parityChildGroup, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize}
For natural numbers $n,r,q$, a group index $g\in\{0,\ldots,r^q-1\}$, and a sign
assignment $a$ on $r$ coordinates, take the indices in the next layer for which there is
a coordinate $j$ such that the index belongs to the child group of $g$ at $j$, and the
product of its normalized block assignment differs from $a(j)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of bottom next-node inputs]
\lean{FABL.mem_parityBottomNextNodeInputs_iff}
\label{FABL.mem_parityBottomNextNodeInputs_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment, FABL.parityBlockProduct, FABL.parityBottomNextNodeInputs, FABL.parityChildGroup, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,r,q$ be natural numbers, let $g$ be an index in a set of size $r^q$, and let $a$
assign a sign in $\{\pm1\}$ to each of $r$ positions. An index $i$ in the layer of size
$r^{q+1}2^r$ belongs to the bottom next-node input set for $(g,a)$ if and only if, under
the canonical indexing of that layer by a pair consisting of an index and a sign
assignment, there is a position $j$ such that the first component is the child index
associated to $(g,j)$ and the product of the signs in the second component, after
replacing signs at positions whose corresponding coordinate is outside the first $n$
positions by $+1$, differs from $a(j)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the next parity node inputs]
\lean{FABL.eval_parityBottomNextNodeInputs}
\label{FABL.eval_parityBottomNextNodeInputs}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitGate.evalFinset, FABL.IsValidParityBlockAssignment, FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.exists_apply_ne_of_ne, FABL.mem_parityBottomNextNodeInputs_iff, FABL.normalizeParityBlockAssignment_eq_self, FABL.parityBlockProduct, FABL.parityBlockValue_valid, FABL.parityBottomLayerValues, FABL.parityBottomLayerValues_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.parityBottomNextNodeInputs, FABL.parityChildGroup, FABL.parityChildGroup_val, FABL.parityExactNodeValue, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityTreeAssignment, FABL.parityTreeAssignment_zero_eq_blockValue}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n,r,q$ be natural numbers, let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, let $g$ index one of $r^q$ groups,
and let $a$ assign a sign to each of the $r$ positions in a block. The OR gate applied
to the bottom-layer values at level $q+1$ over the specified input set equals the exact
OR-node value: it is $1$ if $a$ equals the height-$1$ parity-tree assignment for group
$g$, and $-1$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Layer count under an index cast]
\lean{FABL.circuitTail_layerCount_cast}
\label{FABL.circuitTail_layerCount_cast}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitTail, FABL.CircuitTail.layerCount}
\difficulty{3}
Let $m,k$ be natural numbers with $m=k$, and let $T$ be a circuit tail indexed by $m$.
The layer count of $T$ after transporting it along this equality is equal to the layer
count of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Internal node count under an index cast]
\lean{FABL.circuitTail_internalNodeCount_cast}
\label{FABL.circuitTail_internalNodeCount_cast}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitTail, FABL.CircuitTail.internalNodeCount}
\difficulty{3}
Let $m,k$ be natural numbers with $m=k$, and let $T$ be a circuit tail indexed by $m$.
The internal node count of $T$ after transporting it along this equality is equal to the
internal node count of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation under an index cast]
\lean{FABL.circuitTail_eval_cast}
\label{FABL.circuitTail_eval_cast}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitGate, FABL.CircuitTail, FABL.CircuitTail.eval, FABL.Sign}
\difficulty{3}
Let $m,k$ be natural numbers with $m=k$, let $T$ be a circuit tail indexed by $m$, let
$g$ be an AND or OR gate, and let $v:	ext{Fin}(k)	o	ext{Sign}$ assign a sign to each
input. Evaluating the transported tail $T$ on $v$ gives the same sign as evaluating $T$
on the assignment $i	ext{ }\mapsto v(i\text{ cast along }m=k)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the next parity layer]
\lean{FABL.eval_parityNextLayer}
\label{FABL.eval_parityNextLayer}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitGate, FABL.CircuitGate.dual, FABL.CircuitGate.evalFinset, FABL.ParityBlockAssignment, FABL.eval_parityNextNodeInputs, FABL.get_parityNextLayer, FABL.length_parityNextLayer, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityLayerValues, FABL.parityNextActualAssignment, FABL.parityNextLayer, FABL.parityNextNodeInputs}
\difficulty{3}
Let $r,q$ be natural numbers, let $G$ be either an AND or OR gate, let $A$ assign a sign
block to each of the $r^{q+1}$ groups, and choose an index $i$ in a layer of size
$r^q2^r$. Applying the gate dual to $G$ to the specified level-$q+1$ inputs, whose node
values encode agreement with $A$, gives the level-$q$ node value at $i$ for the dual
gate and the assignment whose $j$th sign is the product of the block assigned by $A$ to
child group $(g,j)$, where $g$ is the group component of $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Standard parity circuit tail]
\lean{FABL.parityStandardTail}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityStandardTail}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitGate, FABL.CircuitGate.dual, FABL.CircuitTail, FABL.length_parityNextLayer, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityNextLayer, FABL.parityOutputInputs}
For a natural number $r$, define the circuit tail $T_{r,q,g}$ for each natural number
$q$ and each gate $g\in\{\mathsf{AND},\mathsf{OR}\}$ recursively as follows. At level
$q=0$, $T_{r,0,g}$ is the singleton output layer whose incoming wires are selected by
the parity product rule for $g$. At level $q+1$, $T_{r,q+1,g}$ consists of the next
layer of parity nodes followed by $T_{r,q,g^*}$, where $g^*$ interchanges AND and OR.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Layer count of the parity circuit tail]
\lean{FABL.parityStandardTail_layerCount}
\label{FABL.parityStandardTail_layerCount}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitGate, FABL.CircuitTail.layerCount, FABL.parityStandardTail}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $r$ and $q$ and a gate $g$ that is either AND or OR, the parity
circuit tail constructed with parameters $r$, $q$, and $g$ has layer count $q+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Internal nodes in the parity circuit tail]
\lean{FABL.parityStandardTail_internalNodeCount}
\label{FABL.parityStandardTail_internalNodeCount}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitGate, FABL.CircuitTail.internalNodeCount, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityStandardTail}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $r$ and $q$ and either an AND or an OR gate, the number of internal
nodes in the parity circuit tail with parameter $r$, depth parameter $q$, and that
output gate is $\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}(r^k 2^r)$, with the sum understood to be zero when
$q=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity bottom next layer]
\lean{FABL.parityBottomNextLayer}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityBottomNextLayer}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityBottomNextNodeInputs, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize}
For natural numbers $n,r,q$, form a list with one entry for each index in a layer of
size $r^q2^r$. The entry at each index is the finite set of inputs to its corresponding
bottom next-layer node, in a layer of size $r^{q+1}2^r$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Length of the Bottom Next Layer]
\lean{FABL.length_parityBottomNextLayer}
\label{FABL.length_parityBottomNextLayer}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityBottomNextLayer, FABL.parityLayerSize}
\difficulty{1}
For all natural numbers $n$, $r$, and $q$, the bottom next layer has length $r^q 2^r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Entries of the normalized parity next layer]
\lean{FABL.get_parityBottomNextLayer}
\label{FABL.get_parityBottomNextLayer}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.length_parityBottomNextLayer, FABL.parityBottomNextLayer, FABL.parityBottomNextNodeInputs, FABL.parityLayerEquiv, FABL.parityLayerSize}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,r,q\in\mathbb N$, and let $i$ be an index in a layer of size $r^q2^r$. Under the
canonical indexing of that layer by pairs $(g,a)$, where $g\in\{0,\ldots,r^q-1\}$ and
$a$ assigns a sign $\pm1$ to each of the $r$ positions, the entry of the normalized
next-layer list at index $i$ is the set of child indices corresponding to pairs $(h,b)$
for which there is some $j\in\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$ such that $h$ is the child group of $g$
and $j$, and the product of the signs in $b$, after replacing entries beyond position
$n$ by $1$, differs from $a(j)$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n,r,q$ be natural numbers, let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, and choose an index $i$ in a layer
of size $r^q2^r$. The OR gate applied to the specified inputs from the bottom layer at
level $q+1$ has the same sign as the OR node at index $i$ in level $q$, whose actual
assignment is the assignment of parity-tree values at height $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity padded circuit tail]
\lean{FABL.parityPaddedTail}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityPaddedTail}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitTail, FABL.length_parityBottomNextLayer, FABL.parityBottomNextLayer, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityStandardTail}
For natural numbers $n,r,q$, form a circuit tail whose first layer is the bottom next
layer and whose remaining tail is the standard parity tail at level $q$ with OR as its
output gate. The resulting tail has input indices in a layer of size $r^{q+1}2^r$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Layer count of the padded parity tail]
\lean{FABL.parityPaddedTail_layerCount}
\label{FABL.parityPaddedTail_layerCount}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitTail.layerCount, FABL.parityPaddedTail}
\difficulty{3}
For natural numbers $n$, $r$, and $q$, the padded parity tail with parameters $n$, $r$,
and $q$ has exactly $q+2$ layers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Internal node count of the padded tail]
\lean{FABL.parityPaddedTail_internalNodeCount}
\label{FABL.parityPaddedTail_internalNodeCount}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitTail.internalNodeCount, FABL.parityLayerSize, FABL.parityPaddedTail, FABL.parityStandardTail_internalNodeCount}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $n,r,q$, the internal node count of the padded parity tail is the
sum of the parity layer sizes from level $0$ through level $q$, namely $\sum_{k=0}^{q}
r^k2^r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity depth circuit from blocks]
\lean{FABL.parityDepthCircuitFromBlocks}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityDepthCircuitFromBlocks}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CircuitTail, FABL.DepthCircuit, FABL.length_parityFirstLayer, FABL.parityFirstLayer, FABL.parityPaddedTail}
For natural numbers $n,r,q$, form a depth circuit on $n$ coordinates whose first layer
consists of the parity terms at level $q+1$, with AND as its gate. Its remaining layers
are the padded parity tail at level $q$, with the layer sizes matched at the join.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Parity tree index bijection]
\lean{FABL.parityTreeIndexEquiv}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.parityTreeIndexEquiv}
\leanok
For natural numbers $r$ and $t$, there is a bijection between pairs consisting of an
index in $\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$ and an index in $\{0,\ldots,r^t-1\}$, and indices in
$\{0,\ldots,r^{t+1}-1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Index formula for the parity tree]
\lean{FABL.parityTreeIndexEquiv_val}
\label{FABL.parityTreeIndexEquiv_val}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityTreeIndexEquiv}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $r,t$ and indices $j<r$ and $k<r^t$, the index corresponding to
$(j,k)$ under the canonical bijection from pairs of such indices to indices below
$r^{t+1}$ is $j r^t+k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product of padded parity inputs]
\lean{FABL.prod_paddedParityInput_eq_prod}
\label{FABL.prod_paddedParityInput_eq_prod}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.paddedParityInput}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,m$ be natural numbers with $n\le m$, and let $x$ be a sign vector of length $n$.
Extend it to length $m$ by using its original coordinates in the first $n$ positions and
the sign $1$ thereafter. The product of the resulting $m$ signs equals the product of
the coordinates of $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Parity tree computes full parity]
\lean{FABL.parityTreeValue_eq_parityFunction}
\label{FABL.parityTreeValue_eq_parityFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityFunction, FABL.parityTreeValue, FABL.parityTreeValue_eq_prod_fin, FABL.prod_paddedParityInput_eq_prod}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,r,h$ be natural numbers and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, with $n\le r^h$. The value at
index $0$ of the depth-$h$ parity tree with branching parameter $r$ is the product of
all coordinates of $x$, namely $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n,r,q$ be natural numbers with $n\le r^{q+2}$. The Boolean function computed by the
parity depth circuit built from blocks of size $r$ and parameter $q$ equals the parity
function on all $n$ coordinates, whose value at an input is the product of its
coordinate signs.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound for the sum of parity layer sizes]
\lean{FABL.sum_parityLayerSize_le}
\label{FABL.sum_parityLayerSize_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityLayerSize}
\difficulty{4}
Let $r,h$ be natural numbers with $r\ge1$ and $h>0$, and define the size of layer $k$ to
be $r^k2^r$. The sum of these sizes for $0\le k<h$ is at most $h r^{h-1}2^r$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n,q$ be natural numbers and let $r$ be a positive natural number. The depth circuit
constructed from parity blocks of width $r$ and parameter $q$ has size at most
$(q+2)r^{q+1}2^r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Real root of a natural number]
\lean{FABL.parityRealRoot}
\label{FABL.parityRealRoot}
\leanok
For natural numbers $n$ and $h$, define the real number $r(n,h)=n^{1/h}$, where the
exponent is the reciprocal of $h$ in $\mathbb{R}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Parity block side length]
\lean{FABL.parityBlockSide}
\label{FABL.parityBlockSide}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityRealRoot}
For natural numbers $n$ and $h$, define the parity block side length to be the maximum
of $1$ and the natural-number ceiling of the parity real root of $n$ and $h$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of the real root]
\lean{FABL.parityRealRoot_nonneg}
\label{FABL.parityRealRoot_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityRealRoot}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $n$ and $h$, the real number $n^{1/h}$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Power of the parity real root]
\lean{FABL.parityRealRoot_pow_pred}
\label{FABL.parityRealRoot_pow_pred}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityRealRoot}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $n$ and $h$ with $h>0$, let $r=n^{1/h}$ denote the real number
defined by the real power of $n$ with exponent $1/h$. Then $r^{h-1}=n^{1-1/h}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Parity block side is positive]
\lean{FABL.one_le_parityBlockSide}
\label{FABL.one_le_parityBlockSide}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityBlockSide}
\difficulty{1}
For all natural numbers $n$ and $h$, let $r=n^{1/h}$ and let the parity block side be
the maximum of $1$ and the natural-number ceiling of $r$. This block side is at least
$1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Real root bounded by block side]
\lean{FABL.parityRealRoot_le_blockSide}
\label{FABL.parityRealRoot_le_blockSide}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityBlockSide, FABL.parityRealRoot}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $n$ and $h$, let $r=n^{1/h}$ and let $b$ be the larger of $1$ and
the least natural number greater than or equal to $r$. Then $r\le b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Parity block side bound]
\lean{FABL.parityBlockSide_le_root_add_one}
\label{FABL.parityBlockSide_le_root_add_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityBlockSide, FABL.parityRealRoot, FABL.parityRealRoot_nonneg}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $n$ and $h$, let $R=n^{1/h}$ and let $B=\max(1,\lceil R\rceil)$,
where the ceiling is the least natural number at least $R$. Then $B\le R+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Parity block side bound]
\lean{FABL.parityBlockSide_pow_covers}
\label{FABL.parityBlockSide_pow_covers}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.parityBlockSide, FABL.parityRealRoot, FABL.parityRealRoot_le_blockSide, FABL.parityRealRoot_nonneg}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $n$ and $h$ with $h>0$, let $s$ be the maximum of $1$ and the least
natural number greater than or equal to $n^{1/h}$. Then $n\le s^h$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Circuit width bound]
\lean{FABL.DepthCircuit.width_le_dimension}
\label{FABL.DepthCircuit.width_le_dimension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula.width_le_iff, FABL.DNFTerm.width_le_dimension, FABL.DepthCircuit, FABL.DepthCircuit.width}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $C$ be a depth circuit on $n$ coordinates,
whose first-layer gates are terms with pairwise distinct literal coordinates. The
maximum number of literals in any first-layer term is at most $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical parity circuit bounds]
\lean{FABL.hasDepthCircuit_parity_canonical}
\label{FABL.hasDepthCircuit_parity_canonical}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DepthCircuit.HasDepthCircuit, FABL.DepthCircuit.width_le_dimension, FABL.depth_parityDepthCircuitFromBlocks, FABL.one_le_parityBlockSide, FABL.parityBlockSide, FABL.parityBlockSide_pow_covers, FABL.parityDepthCircuitFromBlocks, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.size_parityDepthCircuitFromBlocks_le, FABL.toBooleanFunction_parityDepthCircuitFromBlocks}
\difficulty{4}
For every pair of natural numbers $n$ and $q$, the parity function on $\{-1,1\}^n$,
given by the product of all $n$ coordinates, has a depth circuit of depth exactly $q+3$,
size at most $(q+2)\\,b^{q+1}2^b$, and width at most $n$, where $b=\max\{1,\lceil
n^{1/(q+2)}\rceil\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical parity circuit size bound]
\lean{FABL.canonicalParityCircuit_size_real_le}
\label{FABL.canonicalParityCircuit_size_real_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DepthCircuit.size, FABL.one_le_parityBlockSide, FABL.parityBlockSide, FABL.parityBlockSide_le_root_add_one, FABL.parityDepthCircuitFromBlocks, FABL.parityRealRoot, FABL.parityRealRoot_nonneg, FABL.size_parityDepthCircuitFromBlocks_le}
\difficulty{4}
For all natural numbers $n$ and $q$, the size of the canonical parity depth circuit
built with block side $\max(1,\lceil n^{1/(q+2)}\rceil)$ is at most
$(q+2)(n^{1/(q+2)}+1)^{q+1}2^{n^{1/(q+2)}+1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Depth-three parity circuit bounds]
\lean{FABL.hasDepthCircuit_parity_depth_three}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.hasDepthCircuit_parity_depth_three}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DepthCircuit.HasDepthCircuit, FABL.hasDepthCircuit_parity_canonical, FABL.parityBlockSide, FABL.parityFunction}
\proofstep

  {FABL.hasDepthCircuit_parity_canonical}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b001,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p103-b002,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p104-b001}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, the parity function on $\{-1,1\}^n$, given by the
product of all $n$ coordinates, has a depth circuit of depth exactly $3$, size at most
$2b\\,2^b$, and width at most $n$, where $b=\max\{1,\lceil n^{1/2}\rceil\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Has depth circuit parity depth two]
\lean{FABL.hasDepthCircuit_parity_depth_two}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b009}

\begin{theorem}[General parity circuit bounds]
\lean{FABL.hasDepthCircuit_parity_general}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p108-b010}
\label{FABL.hasDepthCircuit_parity_general}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DepthCircuit.HasDepthCircuit, FABL.hasDepthCircuit_parity_canonical, FABL.hasDepthCircuit_parity_depth_two, FABL.parityBlockSide, FABL.parityFunction}
\difficulty{4}
For every pair of natural numbers $n$ and $d$ with $2\le d$, the parity function on
$\{-1,1\}^n$, given by the product of all $n$ coordinates, has a depth circuit of
depth exactly $d$, size at most $(d-1)b^{d-2}2^b$, and width at most $n$, where
$b=\max\{1,\lceil n^{1/(d-1)}\rceil\}$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $f,g$ be sign-valued functions on
$\{-1,1\}^n$. The uniform probabilities that $f$ and $g$ agree and that they disagree
sum to $1$.

\begin{theorem}[Parity agreement forces a degree cutoff]
\lean{FABL.parityAgreement_forces_concentration_cutoff}
\label{FABL.parityAgreement_forces_concentration_cutoff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsFourierSpectrumConcentratedUpTo, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_univ_eq_two_mul_parityAgreement_sub_one, FABL.fourierWeight, FABL.fourierWeightAboveReal, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let $\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon,k\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
$0<\varepsilon_0$ and $\varepsilon<4\varepsilon_0^2$. Suppose that, under the uniform
distribution on $\{-1,1\}^n$, $f$ agrees with the parity function on all $n$ coordinates
with probability at least $\tfrac12+\varepsilon_0$. If the sum of the squared Fourier
coefficients of $f$ over subsets of size greater than $k$ is at most $\varepsilon$, then
$n\le k$.
\end{theorem}
